metadata.title: FedRAMP High Baseline — Organization-Defined Parameters (ODPs) and Additional Requirements
metadata.description: FedRAMP defines specific parameter values (ODPs) for many NIST 800-53 controls. This file captures the key FedRAMP-specified values that CSPs must implement. These are NOT optional — FedRAMP auditors (3PAOs) will test against these exact values.

parameters.notes: Accounts inactive for 90 days must be automatically disabled.
Automated mechanisms to support account management.
Automatically disable accounts after 90 days of inactivity.
Lock account for 30 minutes or until unlocked by administrator.
Must display approved use notification before login.
Limit number of concurrent sessions per user.
Initiate session lock after 15 minutes of inactivity.
Terminate session after 30 minutes of inactivity.

parameters.fedramp_value: Must use encrypted VPN or equivalent
parameters.notes: All remote access must be via encrypted channel with MFA.
All wireless must use enterprise-grade encryption.
All users within 60 days of initial access, annually thereafter.

parameters.fedramp_value: Annual + within 60 days of role assignment
parameters.notes: Specialized training for security-relevant roles.
Must log: successful/failed logins, privilege use, object access, policy changes, admin actions, system events.

parameters.fedramp_value: Date/time, event type, user ID, source, outcome, affected object
parameters.notes: Minimum fields for every audit record.

parameters.fedramp_value: Weekly review; real-time alerts for critical events
parameters.notes: Weekly review of audit logs; immediate alerting on suspicious events.
Logs retained 1 year, immediately available for 90 days.
Must follow FedRAMP penetration test guidance.
Must use government or industry hardening baselines.
Component inventory updated at least monthly; automated where possible.
Contingency plan training for designated personnel.
Annual functional testing or tabletop exercise.

parameters.fedramp_value: Required for all privileged and non-privileged access
parameters.notes: MFA for all users; phishing-resistant for privileged.

parameters.fedramp_value: Case sensitive, min 12 chars, 1 upper, 1 lower, 1 digit, 1 special
parameters.notes: Or use NIST 800-63B memorized secret guidance.
Report to US-CERT/CISA within 1 hour for categories per FedRAMP ICP.
National agency check minimum; higher for elevated positions.

parameters.fedramp_value: Monthly OS/infra; monthly web app; annual pen test
parameters.notes: Monthly authenticated scans; results reported in ConMon deliverables.

parameters.fedramp_value: Deny by default; allow by exception
parameters.notes: All boundary traffic denied unless explicitly permitted.
Non-FIPS-validated modules prohibited for federal data.
All federal data encrypted at rest using FIPS modules.

parameters.fedramp_value: Critical: 30 days, High: 60 days, Moderate: 90 days
parameters.notes: Patch timelines from identification/disclosure.
Real-time monitoring with alerting capability.

fedramp_additional_requirements.description: Monthly vulnerability scan results and POA&M updates submitted to FedRAMP PMO. Annual security assessment by 3PAO. Significant Change Requests (SCRs) submitted for boundary changes.

The CSP must clearly define and document the authorization boundary in the SSP, including all components, data flows, interconnections, and inherited controls. The boundary must be approved by the AO.
Maintain an integrated inventory workbook listing all hardware, software, and interconnections within the authorization boundary per FedRAMP template.
Authentication aligns with NIST SP 800-63 Digital Identity Guidelines. AAL2 minimum for all users; AAL3 recommended for privileged access at High.
deliverables: Digital Identity Determination documented in SSP

fedramp_additional_requirements.description: System categorized per FIPS 199 and FIPS 200. For FedRAMP High, the system impact level is High for one or more of confidentiality, integrity, or availability.
